title: Importance of Nutrition in Managing Diabetes and Pre-diabetes
what_it_is: Importance of Nutrition in Managing Diabetes and Pre-diabetes

sections.label: Healthier food choices programmes
sections.summary: HPB works with industry partners to increase healthier food choices through the Healthier Choice Symbol, Healthier Dining Programme and Healthier Ingredient Development Scheme, and expanded the low glycemic index claim.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To support Singaporeans to make better dietary choices, the Health Promotion Board (HPB) has been working with industry partners to increase the availability of healthier food choices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This includes healthier food products under the Healthier Choice Symbol (HCS) programme, the Healthier Dining Programme and the Healthier Ingredient Development Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To support the War against diabetes, the low glycemic index claim under the HCS programme was recently expanded from the cereals category to include convenience meals and the legumes, nuts and seeds categories.

sections.label: Diabetes Risk Assessment tool
sections.summary: The Diabetes Risk Assessment tool was launched on 1 September 2017 to raise awareness of diabetes risk factors and encourage adults aged 18 to 39 to assess their risk.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: While the current recommendation is for those above 40 years old to go for diabetes screening once every three years, we recognise that age is not the only risk factor for diabetes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This is why the Diabetes Risk Assessment (DRA) tool was launched on 1 September 2017 to raise awareness of the risk factors for diabetes and to encourage younger adults aged 18 to 39 to assess their current risk for undiagnosed diabetes.

sections.label: Diabetes Risk Assessment usage
sections.summary: About 44,000 users aged 18 to 39 used the DRA since its launch, around one-fifth were at higher risk, and more data is needed to analyse its impact.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Since its launch on 1 September, about 44,000 users aged 18 to 39 have used the DRA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Around one-fifth of them, or about 8,500, were found to be at higher risk.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We believe DRA is a useful tool to enhance the effectiveness of our screening efforts, but we would need to collect more data over time to analyse its impact and effectiveness.
